champion: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Eyelid
ordered_diagnoses: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Eyelid
Basal Cell Carcinoma of the Eyelid

facts.raw_span: a 4-year history of a left lower eyelid mass
noted by his wife to have recently grown and acquired a crust
a yellowish-brown, well-circumscribed papule was discovered on the central lower eyelid without margin involvement
the tumor had acquired a flakier surface
The specimen measured 0.8 × 0.5 × 0.3 cm
Classic-appearing hyperkeratotic lesion with many pseudohorn cysts
Proliferation of neoplastic squamous cells originated from one lateral end, pushing down into the dermis and involving many hairs
Malignant squamous cells contained eosinophilic cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli; mitotic figures were present
Central areas of clear cell change were periodic acid–Schiff positive and diastase sensitive
Negative results with Alcian blue and mucicarmine stains
Negative immunohistochemical stains for adipophilin and androgen receptor
Ki67 highlighted scattered basal cells and stained about 20% to 40% of tumor cell nuclei

concepts.preferred_label: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Eyelid
concepts.why: The patient's eyelid mass with a 4-year history, recent growth, and crust formation, along with histopathological findings of a hyperkeratotic lesion with pseudohorn cysts and malignant squamous cells, support this diagnosis
The presence of a well-circumscribed papule with a flakier surface, along with histopathological findings of a hyperkeratotic lesion with central areas of clear cell change, suggest this diagnosis

Although less likely, the patient's eyelid mass with a recent growth and crust formation, along with negative immunohistochemical stains for adipophilin and androgen receptor, could suggest this diagnosis

concepts.preferred_label: Basal Cell Carcinoma of the Eyelid
concepts.why: The patient's eyelid mass with a 4-year history and recent growth could be consistent with this common eyelid tumor
The patient's history of a growing and crusting eyelid mass could be related to this precursor lesion
The histopathological findings of a hyperkeratotic lesion with pseudohorn cysts and central areas of clear cell change could suggest this rare benign tumor
The patient's eyelid mass with a recent growth and histopathological findings of a neoplastic squamous cell proliferation could be related to this rare benign tumor
The histopathological findings of a hyperkeratotic lesion with pseudohorn cysts and negative immunohistochemical stains for adipophilin and androgen receptor could suggest this rare benign tumor

rationales.F06: Hyperkeratotic lesion with pseudohorn cysts is characteristic of squamous cell carcinoma and keratoacanthoma.
rationales.F07: Proliferation of neoplastic squamous cells into the dermis is more typical of squamous cell carcinoma than keratoacanthoma.
rationales.F08: Malignant squamous cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli are characteristic of squamous cell carcinoma.
rationales.F10: Negative Alcian blue and mucicarmine stains rule out sebaceous carcinoma.
rationales.F11: Negative immunohistochemical stains for adipophilin and androgen receptor rule out sebaceous carcinoma.
rationales.F12: Ki67 staining of 20-40% of tumor cell nuclei suggests a moderate to high proliferative index, more typical of squamous cell carcinoma.
